text:
Deletion measures model dependence under a particular intervention; sensitivity alone does not establish user relevance or causal preference. [Hooker et al.](https://research.google/pubs/evaluating-feature-importance-estimates/) highlight distribution-shift problems in feature-removal evaluation. Recommended controls for sequential histories: compare targeted deletion against repeated random removals matched on removal count and recency strata; preserve surviving-item order; report deletion curves and targeted-minus-random effects. Separately examine compacted histories and position-preserving masking, documenting padding, attention masks, positional indices and final-state extraction. These interventions change different aspects of the input, so disagreement is diagnostic rather than proof of relevance. Position-preserving masking may itself create unfamiliar inputs.

Keep validation users, positives and the same 99 unique negatives fixed across models and perturbations, with evaluation mode and deterministic tie handling. Sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking, so describe HR@10 as conditional on this benchmark’s candidate protocol; see [Dallmann et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045). Recommended uncertainty reporting: paired user bootstrap within each category, resampling the same users for both conditions, then recomputing the equal-weight four-category macro difference; report 95% intervals and category effects. Such intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates, excluding training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty.

Repeated checkpoint, hyperparameter and architecture selection can overfit validation performance; [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) explain this selection bias. Record every attempted configuration and checkpoint-selection rule. Treat the winning validation score and its bootstrap interval as exploratory: ordinary post-selection bootstrapping does not remove winner’s optimism. Preserve the supplied splits, freeze the selected pipeline, and reserve generalization claims for the host’s independent held-out evaluation.
